note: Sun 23 Aug 2026, ~07:02 SGT — weekend run; explicitly swept Saturday AND Sunday news before anything else. Four items below (#1, #3, #5, #12) are new or materially refreshed with Sat 22 Aug / early-Sun developments: Iran-conflict escalation (Trump: Iran could be bombed 'a little bit more'; new sanctions detail due Monday 24 Aug), Bitcoin's weekend continuation (Friday's $78,335 close, best week since 2024, then a ~$77,012 Saturday level), oil's Friday settle pricing in the Monday sanctions announcement, and an updated Jackson Hole (27-29 Aug) preview. Gold/silver/COMEX and equities are shut over the weekend so no new closes exist for those; the remaining items are the still-live catalysts from Wed-Fri (19-21 Aug) that continue to drive the book. Two lower-relevance items from the prior edition (Tencent capex, hawkish FOMC minutes) were dropped as stale/superseded.

items.headline: Iran conflict escalates over the weekend: Trump says Iran could be bombed 'a little bit more', Tehran vows it 'will not submit', toughest-ever sanctions detail due Monday
items.summary: Saturday 22 Aug saw the US-Iran standoff harden further: Trump said Iran could still be bombed 'a little bit more' as Washington pivots from military action to an economic crackdown, while a senior figure close to Iran's supreme leader vowed Tehran 'will not submit' and called Trump's rhetoric a sign of desperation. Treasury Secretary Bessent told CNBC the US will impose the 'toughest sanctions in history' on Iran and any nation still trading with it, with full details expected Monday 24 Aug. Separately, Iran has allowed some Iraqi oil tankers through Hormuz this week (per Iraq's president), a partial de-escalation signal that sits alongside the harsher rhetoric.
items.actionable: The Monday sanctions announcement is now a concrete, dated catalyst for the gold hedge and for oil-linked names — the mixed signal (harsher rhetoric + Iraqi tankers still transiting) argues against reading this as a clean escalation-only trade; keep the precious-metals sleeve sized for continued volatility into Monday rather than trimming into the weekend.

items.headline: US Treasury doubles long-end bond buybacks — the single biggest cross-asset catalyst of the week
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced the Treasury is at least doubling its liquidity-support buyback operations for 10-30yr securities (from $2bn to $4bn per operation), starting 9 Sep, after the 30yr yield hit a post-2007 high (~5.33%) on federal-debt concerns. Gross US national debt officially crossed $40 trillion on 20 Aug — the fastest trillion-dollar increment on record, just five months after $39T — with debt-service costs now exceeding the defense budget. The buyback announcement pulled the 10yr to 4.647% and the 30yr to 5.196%, and was widely read as a return to monetary accommodation.
items.actionable: This buyback remains the common thread behind the week's gold/silver breakout, the KOSPI round-trip, and the Bitcoin surge that continued into the weekend — a liquidity/debasement trade, not a growth story. Supportive for the silver/gold miners sleeve and the big-cash-pile thesis as real yields fall.

items.headline: Bitcoin's weekend continuation: Friday close $78,335 (best week since 2024), ETF inflows hit $606M, altcoins outrun BTC into Saturday
items.summary: Bitcoin closed Friday 21 Aug at $78,335.19 (+7.26%), its best weekly performance since 2024, as over $4bn of crypto shorts were liquidated across the week and spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $606mn Friday alone — the largest daily inflow since May, with BlackRock's IBIT capturing 83% of it. Ethereum ran to $2,515 (+8.1%) and XRP was the standout altcoin move at +14.6% to $1.4538, a breadth signal analysts read as institutional rather than single-asset speculation. Per .prices.json, Bitcoin pulled back intraday to a Saturday level of ~$77,012 (-1.7% from Friday's close) — a live weekend quote, not a session close, since crypto trades continuously.
items.actionable: The ETF-inflow and short-squeeze mechanics (not just headline momentum) argue this leg is more durable than a pure sentiment spike, but it remains a levered, correlated extension of the same liquidity/debasement trade driving gold — not a diversifier for the precious-metals sleeve. Next scheduled catalysts: Jackson Hole (27-29 Aug, item below) and the Sept 15 CLARITY Act vote.

items.headline: Gold/silver breakout extends into Friday: gold hits a three-month high (~$4,624.10) as the rally proves durable, not a one-off
items.summary: Gold and silver rallied sharply (GLD +3.84%, SLV +4.47%) Wed 19 Aug as the Treasury buyback news pulled real yields down ahead of the FOMC minutes release, while a weaker dollar amplified gains for foreign buyers; miners outperformed (GDX +9.42%, SILJ +9.55%, Barrick +8.82%). The move continued into Friday 21 Aug, with gold up a further ~2% to a three-month high on continued dollar weakness and the fresh $40T debt milestone; per .prices.json, GC=F front-month settled Friday at $4,624.10 (+2.39%) and GLD at $423.36 (+1.95%). COMEX/GLD/SLV are closed over the weekend, so no fresher close exists.
items.actionable: Confirms this is a genuine, multi-day rates/debasement-driven breakout rather than a one-off headline spike. The Monday Iran-sanctions announcement (item #1) and Jackson Hole (item #12) are the next two dated catalysts that could extend or test the move — argues for holding the position through both rather than trimming into the weekend.

items.headline: Oil rises Friday and heads into the weekend pricing in Monday's Iran-sanctions announcement
items.summary: Brent crude settled Friday at $94.39/bbl (+0.65%) and WTI at $87.06/bbl (+0.26%), both up roughly 6% on the week and near their highest since late July, as Trump's threat of sanctions against Iran's trading partners raised expectations of tighter supply ahead of Monday's formal announcement. Oil futures reopen Sunday evening US time (Monday morning Asia) with the sanctions detail and the weekend's harder Iran rhetoric (item #1) as the immediate overhang.
items.actionable: A live, dated catalyst for Monday's Asia-session open — oil/gold correlation has been tight this week on the same Iran/debasement axis, so a sanctions-driven oil spike would likely reinforce rather than compete with the precious-metals sleeve; watch for any Hormuz-linked shipping disruption as the tail risk.

items.headline: KOSPI's near-perfect 2-day round trip explained: chip-stock crash (Wed) then buyback-fueled rebound (Thu), followed by a calmer profit-taking Friday
items.summary: KOSPI fell 5.80% Wed 19 Aug (Samsung -7.82%, SK Hynix -9.75%) on a US 30-year Treasury yield spike plus a Philadelphia Semiconductor Index selloff, then surged 5.89% Thu 20 Aug (nearly erasing the drop) after Samsung and SK Hynix announced massive capital-return plans and the Treasury buyback eased bond-yield fears. Friday 21 Aug was calmer: KOSPI +0.88% to 6,912.95, with retail booking profits for a second straight day (-₩1,165.5bn) while institutions were modest net buyers (+₩248.4bn) and foreigners net sold in aggregate (-₩171.1bn) despite buying over ₩430bn of Samsung specifically.
items.actionable: A leveraged, yield-driven chip-sector round trip, not a structural anomaly — a preview of how violently HK tech (Tencent/SMIC, similarly AI-capex-exposed) can swing on the same yield/AI-capex-jitters axis; treat single-day HSI/SMIC moves this week with the same lens.

items.headline: Rare-earth names reverse sharply higher (MP +9.10%, UUUU +8.92%) on G7 non-China supply-chain push and US government-backed financing
items.summary: Friday's rare-earth rally reversed Thursday's AI-fear-driven selloff on three concrete policy catalysts: G7 leaders agreed to cut reliance on non-bloc (i.e. China) rare-earth suppliers, the Pentagon backed a $500M loan to Phoenix Tailings, and the Department of Energy selected seven critical-mineral processing/battery projects for support. Materials was the S&P 500's strongest sector on the day (+2.09%); MP separately reported Q2 revenue +89% YoY to $108.5M with government price-protection now 14% of revenue, and guided Q3 NdPr production above 1,000 tonnes.
items.actionable: A genuine, government-policy-driven catalyst distinct from Thursday's sentiment-only selloff — reinforces the ex-China rare-earth re-rating thesis (MP, Lynas, USA Rare Earth, Energy Fuels) underlying the watchlist, independent of the AI-capex-fear cycle.

items.headline: Thursday's US equity selloff (S&P -0.87%, VIX +7.52%) driven by AI-capex balance-sheet fears, not rates
items.summary: The WSJ flagged roughly $3 trillion of off-balance-sheet AI infrastructure commitments across nine major tech names, reviving 'AI bubble' concerns even as the 30yr yield eased post-buyback. VIX jumped over 7% to 16.01 and the 10yr climbed toward 4.70% intraday, before both fully reversed Friday. Rare-earth names caught in the same downdraft: MP Materials -2.89%, Energy Fuels -6.40% (also fully reversed Friday, see item above).
items.actionable: An AI-capex-credibility scare, structurally different from the week's rates-driven metals rally — the fact it fully reversed Friday suggests it was sentiment-driven rather than a durable repricing, but expect it to resurface around Jackson Hole and the next round of AI-capex earnings.

items.headline: Alibaba fiscal Q1: revenue beats, profit misses on 75% YoY AI capex surge; rare HK$10.4bn southbound outflow
items.summary: Alibaba reported revenue of RMB268.95bn (+9% YoY, beat) but adjusted net profit of RMB20.72bn missed estimates (vs RMB25.58bn expected) as capex hit RMB67.68bn (+75% YoY) on AI infrastructure spend. Mainland investors made contrarian net additions to Alibaba (HK$2.21bn) even as Hong Kong saw a rare HK$10.4bn single-day southbound net outflow that same session — still the latest confirmed southbound print (20 Aug) as of this weekend run, per flows-investors.json.
items.actionable: The AI-capex-driven margin compression mirrors the US 'off-balance-sheet AI commitments' scare (item above) playing out in HK tech — the contrarian mainland dip-buying is worth tracking as a read on HK tech risk appetite generally.

items.headline: Singapore banks post record/near-record Q2 2026 profits; OCBC crosses S$30 for the first time
items.summary: DBS (S$3.08bn, +9%), OCBC (S$2.22bn, +22%, record) and UOB (S$1.48bn, +10%) all beat estimates, driven by fee/wealth-management income rather than lending margins. OCBC and DBS trade at all-time highs; UOB lags on NIM compression (1.74%, -8bp), cut fee-income guidance, and is divesting UOB Asset Management (announced 5 Aug).
items.actionable: SGX bank strength (OCBC/DBS momentum) is a structural positive for the owner's largest exposure sleeve independent of this week's volatility; UOB's relative weakness warrants closer monitoring versus peers.

items.headline: OCBC Research turns selective on S-REITs as the sector lags the bank-led STI sharply YTD
items.summary: OCBC Group Research maintained a selective stance on S-REITs, citing rate-hike concerns and elevated long-end yields; the iEdge S-REIT Index has returned -3.3% YTD versus +26.8% for the STI, a gap driven almost entirely by the bank rally. Top picks flagged: CapitaLand Ascendas REIT, CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust, Keppel DC REIT, CapitaLand India Trust.
items.actionable: Quantifies a divergence already implicit in this book — SGX banks near record highs while REITs lag badly on rate concerns. If adding to the SGX REIT sleeve, this argues for being selective (data-centre/industrial names) rather than broad REIT beta.

items.headline: Jackson Hole Symposium (27-29 Aug) — new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first keynote lands Fri 28 Aug, framed as a credibility test
items.summary: Jackson Hole runs 27-29 Aug (theme: financial innovation/payments), with Kevin Warsh delivering his first keynote as Fed Chair on Fri 28 Aug — 19 days before the 16 Sep FOMC decision. Warsh, confirmed 54-45 (the closest Fed Chair confirmation vote in US history) and known for a policy of narrowing forward guidance, faces a market that per a BofA survey expects a 69%-neutral tone; TD Securities flagged the speech as a critical moment for Warsh to reestablish Fed inflation credibility, with the August jobs report and CPI still to come before the Sept decision.
items.actionable: The next major scheduled catalyst for gold/silver and rates, now one week out — given Warsh's dissent history favored hikes over cuts, his tone could either validate or puncture the current liquidity/debasement rally in metals and Bitcoin. Size gold/silver-miner and crypto-adjacent positioning with this event in mind.
